title: The 8(a) Reset: What Changed for Black Federal Contractors | Across the Water, Ep. 16
lede: Black-owned small businesses won 1.54% of small-business-eligible federal contract dollars in fiscal 2024, about US$9.83 billion, by a Brookings count. The SBA's 8(a) program, built to widen that door, has been rebuilt: a first full audit, more than 1,000 firms suspended, and since Sep 10, 2026, no presumption of disadvantage for Black Americans or any other group. Ahead of Wednesday's Brookings forum on what replaces 8(a), this episode explains what changed, what it means for Black contractors, and how each side reads it.
keyPoints: Black American-owned small businesses won US$9.83 billion, 1.54% of small-business-eligible prime contract dollars, in FY2024 (Brookings, Mar 26, 2026).
8(a) firms won US$24.3 billion in FY2025, down 5.8% (SBA scorecard data via Washington Technology).

Since Sep 10, 2026, individually owned applicants must show discrimination against their group and material harm; current participants and tribal and other entity-owned firms are unaffected (Federal Register 2026-16370).
SBA suspended more than 1,000 of about 4,300 firms in January 2026 and referred 689 removed firms to GSA for contract audits on Oct 21, 2026 (SBA).
The small disadvantaged business goal was cut from 15% to the statutory 5%; agencies still awarded 11.6% (US$75.3 billion) in FY2025 (ExecutiveGov; Washington Technology).
